modules.module_title: Post - Harvest storage and Lemongrass oil extraction — Core Assessment Criteria

pcs.pc_description: To Harvest lemon grass when it reaches a height of about 2 to 3 feet.
Use sharp and clean pruning shears or a sickle for harvesting.
Cut the leaves above the ground level, leaving the roots intact for regrowth.
To Perform selective harvesting by cutting mature leaves while leaving young and healthy leaves for continued growth.
Harvest in the morning when the oil content in the leaves is higher.
Harvest every 3 to 4 months, depending on the growth rate and climate.
Adjust the frequency based on the health and growth of the lemon grass.
Dry the harvested lemon grass in a well- ventilated area away from direct sunlight.
to preserve the essential oils, Use a drying rack or hang bundles upside down
To retain freshness and aroma. Store dried lemon grass leaves in airtight containers
To avoid contamination, Glass or metal containers are preferred
Store the containers in a cool, dark place to preserve the quality of the dried leaves.
To prevent mold, Protect the lemongrass from moisture
Lemongrass oil is commonly extracted through steam distillation.
To separate the essential oil from the plant material, Use a distillation apparatus
Place the lemongrass in the distillation apparatus, and steam is passed through.
The essential oil is captured, and water condenses separately.
Allow the collected oil to settle, and separate it from the water layer.
The resulting oil is pure lemongrass essential oil.
Store the extracted lemongrass oil in dark- colored glass bottles.
Seal the bottles tightly to prevent exposure to air and light.
